2027-03-31.title: First Wednesday of Resurrection
2027-03-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The faithful are strengthened through prayer
2027-03-31.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The first week of the Resurrection, the week of the newly baptised. The calendar notes the fuller passages: Ephesians 4:1–16 and John 15:1–25.
2027-03-31.verse: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
theo: “I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.” In Easter week these words were sung over the newly baptised, who had just put on white garments. Every Christian has been clothed by God: not with a robe we earned, but with Christ himself. “As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ” (Galatians 3:27). Then Isaiah turns to Zion, the forsaken city, and speaks of a wedding. “You shall no more be termed Forsaken, and your land shall no more be termed Desolate; but you shall be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married; for the LORD delights in you.” “For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.” This is the language of the Easter Church. Christ the Bridegroom has given his life for his bride, the Church, and has risen to rejoice over her. The East Syriac liturgy loves this image: the Church is the bride betrothed to Christ, and the Holy Qurbana is the wedding feast. On Easter, God gives his people a new name: not Forsaken but My Delight. Every baptised person, however unworthy he feels, can hear the Risen Lord say to him: you are my delight.

In Acts, Peter and John have been arrested for healing a lame man in the name of Jesus and for preaching the Resurrection. They are threatened and released. They go back to their friends, and the whole community does not panic or complain; it prays. “When they heard it, they raised their voices together to God and said, ‘Sovereign Lord, who made the heaven and the earth, the sea, and everything in them’.” They read their situation in the light of Psalm 2: the rulers of the earth gathered against the Lord and his Anointed. And they do not ask for the threats to end, or for revenge. They ask for courage: “And now, Lord, look at their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness, while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy servant Jesus.” The answer comes at once: “When they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.” Paul, writing from prison, shows the fruit of that Spirit in the life of the community: “I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to lead a life worthy of the calling to which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, making every effort to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” And he names the sevenfold unity of the Church: “There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to the one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in all.” The persecuted Church is strong when she prays together and when she stays one.

The Gospel is the parable of the vine, spoken at the Last Supper over the cup of wine. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinegrower. He removes every branch in me that bears no fruit. Every branch that bears fruit he prunes to make it bear more fruit.” The key word is ‘abide’, repeated again and again. “Abide in me as I abide in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, neither can you unless you abide in me.” “I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.” The branch does not produce fruit by effort but by staying connected; the sap of the vine does the work. The Risen Christ is not only an example to imitate but a life to share. We abide in him through Baptism, by which we are grafted into the vine; through the Holy Qurbana, in which he says, “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them” (John 6:56); through his word remaining in us; and through keeping his commandments. “As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.” The pruning is not punishment but care: the Father cuts back what is useless so that we may bear more fruit. Many a Christian has found that a time of loss or suffering became a time of greater fruitfulness. The vine of Kerala's ancient Christian community has been pruned many times in its long history, and it still bears fruit in vocations, in missionaries, in families of faith across the world, because it abides in the vine.
conn: “he has clothed me with the garments of salvation” (Isaiah 61:10); the baptised “have clothed yourselves with Christ” (Galatians 3:27); the saints in heaven wear robes made white in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14).

“as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you” (Isaiah 62:5); “Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her” (Ephesians 5:25); John sees the holy city “prepared as a bride adorned for her husband” (Revelation 21:2).

Zion receives “a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give” (Isaiah 62:2); to the one who conquers the Risen Lord gives “a white stone, and on the white stone is written a new name” (Revelation 2:17).
The community prays Psalm 2:1–2 (Acts 4:25–26); the same psalm says, “You are my son; today I have begotten you” (Psalm 2:7), which Paul applies to the Resurrection (Acts 13:33).
“Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread” (1 Corinthians 10:17); “that they may all be one” (John 17:21).
Israel was the vine brought out of Egypt (Psalm 80:8); Isaiah sang of the vineyard that yielded wild grapes (Isaiah 5:1–7); Jesus is the true vine in whom the people of God bears fruit (John 15:1).
altar: The vine was spoken over the cup of the Last Supper. At every Holy Qurbana the fruit of the vine becomes the Blood of Christ, and those who drink it abide in him and he in them.
The one bread and one cup make us one body: the unity Paul begs us to keep is received at the altar before it is lived in the parish.
outline: A vine in a Kerala courtyard, its branches pruned and green again.
My Delight Is in Her: the Bridegroom's joy over his people.
The persecuted Church prays and is filled with the Spirit.
Point 3 · One Lord, one faith, one baptism
Keeping the unity of the Spirit.
The vine, the branches and the pruning.
A small room in Jerusalem shaking as a frightened community finishes its prayer.
“Apart from me you can do nothing.”
live: Stay ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, or ten minutes in silence with the Gospel, simply abiding.
When afraid to speak of your faith, pray the community's prayer: Lord, grant me to speak your word with boldness.
Choose one person in your family or parish who tests your patience, and bear with them in love this week.
Remember those who suffer for Christ today, and pray for them by name where you know of them.
fathers: The branches are in the vine not so as to give anything to the vine, but so as to receive from it the life by which they live; the vine is in the branches to give them life, not to receive it. So it is good for the disciples to abide in Christ, but it adds nothing to him. Cut off, a branch can do nothing; it is fit either for the vine or for the fire.

The Church is the bride whom the Son betrothed to himself on the Cross and adorned with his own Blood. Her wedding garment is the robe of glory she lost in Adam and received again in the water of Baptism. Let her rejoice, for her Bridegroom is risen and lives for ever.
magis: From the beginning Jesus associated his disciples with his own life; the Church is communion with him, as the branches with the vine.
The unity of Christ and the Church, head and members, is expressed by the image of bridegroom and bride.
The Church is one: one Lord, one faith, one Baptism; her unity is kept by charity, the profession of one faith, common worship and apostolic succession.
The Holy Spirit unites the Church to the life of Christ, the vine, so that she may bear fruit.
The first Christian communities prayed intensely for one another; in persecution they asked for boldness to proclaim the Word.
saints: 31 March: St Benjamin, deacon and martyr in Persia (died about 424), a witness of the Church of the East who would not stop speaking of Christ.
2027-03-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true vine, the Father has grafted us into you through Baptism and feeds us with your Body and Blood. Let us abide in you as you abide in us, and let your word remain in us. Prune from us what is useless, so that we may bear much fruit for the glory of the Father. Clothe us with the garments of salvation, keep your Church one in the bond of peace, and give us boldness to speak your word, as you gave it to the apostles when the house was shaken. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: you shall no more be called Forsaken but My Delight; as a bridegroom rejoices, so God rejoices over you.
Acts: threatened, the Church prays for boldness, and the place is shaken.
Jesus: I am the vine, you are the branches; apart from me you can do nothing.
2027-03-31.action: Spend ten minutes today simply abiding with Christ, in church or with the Gospel.
2027-03-31.question: Am I connected to the vine, or am I trying to bear fruit by myself?
kidsaint: He was a deacon in Persia about 1,600 years ago. The king put him in prison for teaching about Jesus, and then let him out on condition that he stop. But Benjamin said he could not stop telling people about Jesus, and he died as a martyr. Lesson: like the apostles, ask Jesus for courage to speak about him!
2027-03-31.special: First Wednesday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: A Greek word used in Acts for the courage and freedom with which the apostles spoke of Christ (Acts 4:29, 31). It is a gift of the Holy Spirit, given in answer to prayer.

family.explain: Jesus said: “I am the vine, you are the branches.” A vine is a plant like the grape plant. The branches get all their life from the plant. If a branch is cut off, it dries up. If it stays on the plant, it grows grapes! We stay close to Jesus by praying, going to Holy Qurbana, and loving others. Then we can do good things, like a branch full of fruit.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always stay close to Jesus, like branches on the vine.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to stay close to Jesus?”

illus: An old man in Kuravilangad kept a pepper vine climbing up a jackfruit tree behind his house. Every year after the harvest he cut it back hard, and his grandson, visiting from Bengaluru, thought he was destroying it. ‘Wait and see,’ said the grandfather. By the next season the vine was thick with green spikes of pepper. One evening the grandfather showed the boy a single branch that had been broken off in a storm and lay on the ground. It was dry and black. ‘Same vine, same rain, same sun,’ he said. ‘Only one thing was different: it was no longer attached.’ The boy remembered that when, years later, he found himself far from home and far from the Church, and he went back.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true vine, we are your branches. Let your life flow in us as we gather in your name. Amen. Alleluia!
share: He has clothed me with the garments of salvation (Isaiah 61:10). Do I live as one clothed with Christ?
Grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness (Acts 4:29). Where do I need courage to witness?
Bearing with one another in love (Ephesians 4:2). Whom do I find hard to bear with?
Abide in me as I abide in you (John 15:4). What helps me to abide, and what cuts me off?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For the unity of the Church, that all Christians may be one in Christ.
For Christians persecuted for their faith, that they may be filled with the Holy Spirit and speak with boldness.
For the newly baptised, that they may remain in Christ and bear much fruit.
For those who are being pruned by suffering, that they may trust the Father's care.
For our parish, that it may be one body, bearing with one another in love.
pm.close: Father, you are the vinegrower who prunes the branches so that they may bear more fruit. Keep us in your Son, the true vine, fill us with the Holy Spirit, and make us one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah sings: “I will greatly rejoice in the LORD… for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation.” The newly baptised wore white this week. All of us were clothed with Christ in Baptism. And God speaks to his people as a bridegroom: “You shall no more be termed Forsaken… but you shall be called My Delight Is in Her.” Each of us can hear the Risen Lord say: you are my delight.

In Acts, Peter and John are threatened for preaching Jesus. The community gathers and prays. They do not ask God to remove the threats; they ask for boldness: “grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness.” And the place is shaken, and they are filled with the Holy Spirit.

Paul writes from prison: lead a life worthy of your calling, “with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love.” There is one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. A Church that prays together and stays one cannot be defeated.

And Jesus says: “I am the vine, you are the branches… apart from me you can do nothing.” A branch does not bear fruit by trying harder, but by staying attached. We stay attached to him through prayer, through his word, through keeping his commandments, and above all through the Holy Qurbana: “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.”
Sometimes the Father prunes us. It hurts. But he cuts only to make us bear more fruit. Many of us can look back and see that a hard time was a fruitful time.

This week, let us abide. Ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, or ten minutes with the Gospel. Let us ask for boldness to speak of Jesus, and bear patiently with one difficult person. Apart from him we can do nothing; with him we bear much fruit. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: ‘I am the vine, you are the branches.’ A branch stays green and grows fruit only when it is joined to the plant.
We stay joined to Jesus when we pray, go to Holy Qurbana and love others. Let us stay close to Jesus every day!

intro: Theme: “I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.”
The bride clothed with salvation, the Church praying for boldness, the unity of the Spirit, and the true vine.

concl: The Risen Christ is the Bridegroom who delights in us and the vine who gives us life.
Abide in him, pray for boldness, keep the unity of the Spirit, and you will bear much fruit.
